title: Is organic farming always good for the environment?
summary: Short research summary: organic farming can raise on-farm biodiversity but needs more land, so the net benefit depends on context.

assertions.quote: organic farming can lead to increased biodiversity compared to Conventional farming

verdicts.note: Citing earlier studies, Clark and Tilman say on-farm and near-farm biodiversity tends to be higher under organic, probably from lower fertilizer and pesticide inputs, but warn that at larger scales the extra land clearing could make the net effect negative.

assertions.quote: it can also require more land to produce the same yield of crops
